correctness.rationale: The frozen norms and rigidity are mathematically correct; the repair narrows the distinct contribution, not the mathematical identities. QP_R is finite rank. For the reverse norm inequality, a near-norming tail input can be restricted to the finitely many coordinates used by a near-norming output level without increasing input norm. The resulting sequence lives in the level c0-sum and escapes every finite set of levels; every full-space functional restricts to an ell1 family there, so the sequence is weakly null in the full space. Compact operators send it to zero in norm. This proves the exact tail identity; the argument is not valid for arbitrary bounded operators without locality. At fixed output level finite-p duality gives c_n^(-1/p) times the dual optimization and each input support function contributes c_l^(1/p) times the conjugate-space norm. This includes p=1; at p=infinity the row phases give the absolute grouped sum exactly. At the endpoint each retained row induces a partition of a subset of the finite coefficient list; its possible norms form a finite set and the supremum belongs to it. The monotone sequence stabilizes, and compactness forces its eventual value to be zero, whence Q=QP_R and finite rank. The converse is immediate. For Liu–Ma's example the two-coordinate norm factor is 2^(1-1/p), the normalized sphere ratio is q^(-ceil(n/2)), and the first admissible n for large R is 2(R+1); at infinity every surviving row has norm 2. This confirms both iterated limits. The replacement's finite-p re-representation is also valid: sign-randomize the finitely many used inputs at a level; Jensen conditional on one group's image sign bounds that group's p-norm by ||Q||/|b_G|. Complete each group map by root values, then subtract the excess root term with a single root map because the sum of the present groups' coefficients is row independent. This verifies the same operator class in a different presentation. The frozen 3,494 assertions are supplementary recorded checks, not a fresh run or a proof of the tail principle.
